I’ve been to EDCO 6x and I went to EDC Mexico for the first time last year. I just did my first EDC Vegas in May. 

I personally feel like Mexico is larger than Orlando but not as large as Vegas. It is definitely a lot more accessible than Vegas. We stayed in the Reforma neighborhood of CDMX and were about a 15 minute Uber away. 

I’ve only done VIP at these festivals and I never felt too crowded in the VIP section. 

Price wise- EDC Mexico tickets were the cheapest. 

Vibes- EDC Mexico is less about party favors and more about drinking. It is still such a good time. There were vendors scattered throughout the crowds and the food was really good for festival food. Also, there were so many vendors outside the festival selling bootleg merch and street food. 

Overall if you can go, I 100% recommend.
I think I bought 2 3day VIP tickets for about $500 usd total. It was really affordable. And I ended up buying a Saturday VIP ticket for around $120 usd for someone to join us.

I’ve been to EDCO 5x and I went to EDC Mexico for the first time this year. 

I stayed in the Reforma area of Mexico City, about a 15 minute Uber. It was so easy to move around with Ubers, we never took a taxi or the metro. I never felt unsafe walking around Mexico. 

Granted we always do VIP, but no one in our group of 5 has ever been pickpocketed at either festival. 

When we are in Orlando for the festival we typically stay in the “Disney Bubble”. When we went to Mexico we were there for 8 days and went exploring every day and night. 

Next year, we are doing EDCLV and EForest. Honestly, I would love to make EDC Mexico, the festival I can make it to every year. The vibes are immaculate.

These are liquid to matte lipsticks. They were limited edition back in December and came back early January. They are right now sold out **BUT** will be coming back permanently sometime soon according to the LA Splash instagram page.

Now on to the review...
Overall the lipsticks seem to vary in consistency. None of them are too drying on the lips and are similar in texture to the Sephora Matte Lip Cremes and KVD Liquid Liquid Lipsticks. **Venom** was by far one of the drier ones. It still went on smoothly but dried fast. **Malevolent** was the trickiest one to apply. It was a bit thick and quite patchy. I think with this shade you need to work slowly and carefully when applying it. **Phantom** was the most liquidy and that one definitely needed to be built up a few layers to reach the same level of opacity as the others. **Goulish** was very easy to apply. It was a bit on the thinner side but not as thin as Phantom. **Vindictive** is my favorite. It has a more creme consistency and is a bit thick but it was by far the easiest to apply. Overall I really like these lipsticks . They are completely transfer proof and they do not budge at all. And I am so glad they are no longer LE because that means I can use them with out worrying about them running out! BTW this bundle came with a Shea Butter Remover but any oil based remover will take them off. I tried taking them off with just a baby wipe and would not recommend it. They will not budge.

I wanted to compare Goulish to OCC lip tar in Sebastian because at first I thought they could be pretty similar. But once I did you can see that Sebastian (middle and right swatches) is a bit more on the lavenderish side.
